old_findings.note: The command-executed key prints as sha3(0x957705a3..., _279) in the duplicate check, the set and the reset after a failed command (stor4[sha3(...)] = 0), no more raw-memory hashes.

regressions.source: AxelarGateway.sol execute: commandHash = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(commands[i])); if (commandHash == SELECTOR_DEPLOY_TOKEN) ... (6-way dispatch)
regressions.issue: _280 and _281 are reads of mem[64] with no store to it in between (equal), but their difference is no longer folded, so the six command-hash tests carry the length '_280 - _281 + _287' and base _281. Same root cause as the c00063 regression (16 texts corpus-wide).
regressions.rule: Reads of mem[64] with no store to mem[64] between them hold the same value: one symbol, so '_a - _b' folds to 0.

regressions.decompiled: if idx >= mem[32 * _17 + ceil32(_1) + ceil32(cd[transactionBytecode + cd[transactionBytecode + 36] + 36]) + ceil32(cd[transactionBytecode + cd[transactionBytecode + 68] + 36]) + 316]:
regressions.source: AxelarGateway.sol execute: (..., bytes32[] memory commandIds, string[] memory commands, bytes[] memory params) = abi.decode(data, ...)
regressions.issue: The commands array pointer _23 is expanded into its 150-character allocation expression at each use.
regressions.rule: Keep a variable for a held mem[64] value whose expression is long; substitute only short ones.

improvements: Round-1 finding fixed (command-executed key); events with several dynamic arguments decoded exactly (ContractCall / ContractCallWithToken: string destinationChain=Array(...), string destinationContractAddress=Array(...), bytes payload=Array(...); TokenMintLimitUpdated(symbol=Array(...), limit)); a revert's bytes argument split into length and data; the duplicate check reads _17 != _22 or _17 != mem[_45]; P6 8 -> 0.
notes: Diff of 551 lines read in full on its substantive lines (function counts unchanged; burnToken only moved). The dispatch, the self-call and the Executed event are unchanged.
summary: Minor regressions in execute: an unfolded difference of two equal mem[64] reads in the six command-hash tests, and the commands array pointer expanded into a long address. Otherwise better: the command-executed key is resolved everywhere and the events' dynamic arguments are decoded.
